article.summary: GitHub Agentic Workflows (gh-aw) compiles Markdown workflow definitions into GitHub Actions workflows and offers file-backed memory through Actions cache, Git branches, and an experimental GitHub Drives preview.

who_what.text: The official repository presents GitHub Agentic Workflows as an open-source GitHub CLI extension and compiler. The reviewed memory features are workflow storage integrations rather than a separate memory server.

architecture.text: The project compiles Markdown workflow source with YAML frontmatter into GitHub Actions workflows. Memory directories are plain files managed by generated setup and persistence steps around agent execution.

Cache-memory stores workflow files in Actions cache, repo-memory persists files in Git branches, and experimental Drive memory mounts GitHub Drives for enrolled preview repositories. None of the inspected guides imposes a common fact schema.

Current canonical repository is github/gh-aw, default branch main, reviewed at full head ea7bc4dd637ff9c9f61e1706a53041c34cd4724c. Reviewed 2026-11-25 20:55:28 UTC (12:55:28 PST; America/Los_Angeles).

behavior.text: The agent writes ordinary files in configured memory directories. Cache-memory saves into cache lineages; repo-memory validates and commits/pushes eligible files; Drive memory checks out and later publishes validated drive changes. Optional schema and JavaScript validators, extension/glob filters, and size/count/patch limits constrain persistence.

Files may be overwritten or removed locally, and repo-memory keeps Git history. The guides do not establish content-level correction, tombstones, or physical erasure across caches, branch history, backups, and external drive storage. Repo-memory preserves existing branch files outside its configured eligible-file scope.

The reviewed guides expose file mounts and prompt instructions, not a built-in semantic recall API. The agent or separately configured tools must locate and interpret relevant files; retrieval quality is unknown.

Cache memory uses branch/key lineages, with optional integrity levels and default-branch fallback. Repo memory uses configured branches and target repositories. Drive scope is repository/ref/drive based in the preview. These boundaries do not prove adversarial isolation; Drive service-side namespace enforcement is not verified by gh-aw.

Repo Git history and cache integrity branches can expose writer lineage, while threat detection and validation can gate some writes. Memory remains untrusted: these controls do not authenticate truth or establish claim-level evidence, and cache contents are unsigned and unverified.

Guides document workflow logs, validation output and persistence job summaries. Cache memory has a 10GB per-repository quota and seven-day inactivity eviction; repo memory has file/count/patch constraints and repository limits. No runtime efficiency measurements were collected.

metrics.text: Answerable recall and abstention — unmeasured; file mounting and agent retrieval are documented, but no retrieval workload was scored.
Correction accuracy and stale-value rate — unmeasured; files can be updated and versioned, but no correction workload was run.
Deletion leakage — unmeasured; no end-to-end physical erasure guarantee was established or probed.
Scope-isolation leakage — unmeasured; storage scopes are documented, but no cross-scope workload was executed.
Evidence support and citation coverage — unmeasured; the inspected memory guides do not define claim-level citations and no answer adjudication was done.
Retrieval latency, write-to-recall delay, tokens, cost, and storage efficiency — unmeasured; no system or benchmark workload was run.

limits: Bounded review of current official README, cache/repository/Drive memory documentation, prompt templates, and selected cache setup/commit and repository clone source. Other compiler paths, jobs, and external service behaviors were not exhaustively traced.
No gh-aw runtime, tests, or benchmarks were executed. Runtime correctness, recall quality, complete deletion, adversarial isolation, latency, token use, cost, and storage efficiency remain unknown.

The documented file-oriented model delegates memory schema, recall selection, and evidence quality to workflows and agents; no general-purpose fact correction or evidence adjudication mechanism was established.
Drive memory is explicitly experimental and available only to repositories admitted to the GitHub Drives private preview.

benchmark.note: No gh-aw runtime, tests, or benchmark workload was executed. No metric values are claimed.
